description: §17.4a (S308) — a braceless (unparenthesized) `for x of @items { ... }` loop head, written without the parentheses the canonical `for (x of @items) { ... }` form requires, fires E-FOR-UNPARENTHESIZED-HEAD. The braceless-head parse branch consumes only the legacy English `in` form; a braceless `of` is not consumed, so `collectExpr` mis-reads the iterable as the bare token `of` and codegen would emit `for (const x of of)` (valid to `node --check`, a `ReferenceError` at module-eval). Reject + recover: fires ONCE per offending head, then recovers by consuming `of` and collecting the real iterable so no broken loop is emitted. Wrapped in a `${ ... }` logic block, so E-CONTROL-FLOW-IN-MARKUP (which fires on bare markup control-flow and requires a parenthesized `(...){` head) does NOT co-fire. W-PROGRAM-001 co-fires incidentally (no `<program>` shell); not asserted.
rationale: §34 E-FOR-UNPARENTHESIZED-HEAD: a braceless `for … of` loop head SHALL be rejected. §17.4a `**Syntax:**` mandates the parenthesized head `for (let x of collection) { ... }`; without the parentheses the iterable is mis-read as the bare token `of` and the loop ships broken. Reject + recover: the head is parsed as if parenthesized so no broken loop reaches the output. §34 registers the code at severity Error and partitions it into result.errors.
